verifiedAgainst: Intune service release current as of July 2026; Jamf Pro 11.x
notes: Perishable data. Advisory notes are held per target MDM — 'toIntune' applies when Intune is the destination, 'toJamf' when Jamf is. Live evidence from the tenants and from Intune's settings catalog always overrides these entries; they exist for the things an API can't tell you. Re-verify before relying on a gap report.

toIntune.notes: Fallback path for anything unmapped.

toJamf.notes: Upload the plist or mobileconfig directly.
Code requirements must be re-generated if app signing differs.

toIntune.notes: Kernel extensions are legacy; map to system extensions.

toJamf.notes: Team identifiers and bundle identifiers carry over unchanged; Jamf edits them in a native payload.
Jamf exposes firewall settings in the Security & Privacy payload rather than as a standalone firewall object.
Gatekeeper assessment lives alongside firewall settings in the same Jamf payload.
Several distinct Jamf payloads share this domain — check which keys you actually need.

toIntune.notes: Font files must be under 2 MB.

toJamf.notes: Font files must be re-uploaded.
Jamf has a dedicated editor covering banner text, user list visibility and power-button behaviour.
Idle time and password-on-wake sit in the Login Window payload; per-user screensaver settings are a separate payload.

toIntune.notes: Several intelligence-related keys deprecated in OS 26.4; use DDM configurations instead.

toJamf.notes: Jamf's Restrictions editor exposes a subset of the domain; anything missing goes through Application & Custom Settings.

profilePayloads.impact: Recovery keys do not migrate in either direction. The destination MDM cannot escrow a key it never issued, so keys must be re-issued and re-escrowed after the move.

toIntune.notes: See disruptionItems for the re-escrow path.

toJamf.notes: Jamf issues its own recovery key via the Disk Encryption configuration; existing keys don't transfer. See disruptionItems.

profilePayloads.impact: Users must re-register Platform SSO after the move, whichever MDM they land on.

toIntune.notes: Registration is driven by the Company Portal.

toJamf.notes: Jamf Connect or a Kerberos extension may be required depending on the identity provider.

profilePayloads.impact: Certificate identities used for 802.1X do not transfer. Stage them in the destination before moving devices or they lose network on arrival.

toIntune.notes: Pair with a SCEP or PKCS profile for the identity.

toJamf.notes: Pair with a Jamf-issued certificate payload for the identity.

profilePayloads.impact: Per-app VPN mappings and certificate identities need rebuilding in the destination.

toJamf.notes: Jamf edits VPN natively, but the certificate identity must be reissued through Jamf PKI before the profile will connect.

profilePayloads.impact: Certificates are issued by the MDM's own CA connector. They do not move; they are reissued.

toIntune.notes: Requires the Intune Certificate Connector.

toJamf.notes: Requires a Jamf PKI or AD CS integration.

profilePayloads.impact: SCEP identities are issued by the MDM's CA connector and are reissued rather than migrated.

toIntune.notes: Built from the Intune profile template, not the settings catalog. Requires the Intune Certificate Connector and an NDES/SCEP endpoint.

toJamf.notes: Jamf can proxy SCEP requests or hand the device a direct SCEP URL.
Jamf manages login items natively; paths must exist on the target device or the item is silently skipped.

toIntune.equivalent: Settings catalog > Login > Login Window Login Items

toJamf.notes: Delivered through the Login Window payload in Jamf.

toIntune.notes: Auto-enables and auto-allows matched background items.

toJamf.notes: No native Jamf editor. Deliver the Rules array through Application & Custom Settings.

toIntune.notes: Includes On Demand rules and encrypted DNS protocol settings.

toJamf.notes: Jamf edits encrypted DNS natively, including On Demand rules.

toIntune.notes: Intune exposes only the declarative configurations Microsoft has implemented; it cannot deliver an arbitrary custom DDM declaration. Anything outside that set has to be rebuilt with the settings it does support.

toJamf.notes: Jamf Pro delivers declarative configurations through Blueprints. Check which declaration types your Jamf version exposes.

toIntune.notes: Re-upload the certificate; the profile carries no secret.

toJamf.notes: Re-upload the certificate; the profile carries no secret.

toIntune.notes: Complex Dock layouts usually need a custom profile.

toJamf.notes: Jamf has a full Dock editor including persistent apps and folders, so complex layouts survive better in this direction.

toIntune.notes: Rebuild as a declarative configuration. The legacy payload, MDM update commands and update restrictions are being removed with the 2026 OS release.

toJamf.notes: Jamf's own update controls have moved to declarative enforcement; confirm what your Jamf Pro version exposes before rebuilding.

toIntune.notes: Deferral keys are superseded by declarative enforcement.

toJamf.notes: Deferral keys are superseded by declarative enforcement.

toIntune.notes: Not confirmed against current docs. Verify before relying on this entry.

toJamf.notes: Jamf manages printers as their own object as well as via payload.

toIntune.notes: No equivalent in Intune. Directory binding is largely obsolete on macOS — consider Platform SSO instead.

toJamf.notes: Jamf still exposes a Directory binding payload, though binding is largely obsolete on macOS.

toIntune.notes: Re-upload required; Intune wraps PKGs and requires them signed with a Developer ID Installer certificate.

toJamf.notes: Re-upload to a Jamf distribution point. Jamf can deploy unsigned packages, so this direction is less restrictive.

toIntune.notes: One value per script, and Intune expects a single echoed value. Jamf EA output usually needs trimming.

toJamf.notes: Jamf accepts richer output and supports data types and inventory display, so custom attribute scripts usually port with little change.

toIntune.notes: No parameters, no event triggers, and a per-tenant script count limit. Values must be hardcoded.

toJamf.notes: Jamf regains parameters ($4-$11) and event triggers, so an Intune shell script can usually be simplified rather than rewritten.

toIntune.notes: Different syntax and evaluation model: Entra evaluates directory attributes, not device inventory. Inventory-based criteria have no equivalent.

toJamf.notes: Jamf evaluates device inventory directly, so most Entra dynamic rules must be rewritten against inventory attributes instead.

toIntune.notes: Intune has no event-triggered policy engine. Rebuild as scheduled shell scripts, app assignments or settings catalog policies.

toJamf.notes: Moving to Jamf, scheduled Intune scripts can become real policies with triggers, scoping and Self Service availability.

toIntune.notes: Company Portal customisation is far more limited: no categories, branding or per-item descriptions to the same degree.

toJamf.notes: Jamf Self Service is considerably richer, so this direction gains capability rather than losing it.

toIntune.notes: No Intune equivalent for third-party patch definitions.

toJamf.notes: Jamf provides patch definitions and reporting that Intune has no counterpart for.

toIntune.notes: No Intune equivalent. Blocking application launch requires a different approach entirely.

toJamf.notes: Jamf can block application launch by process name, which Intune cannot.

toIntune.notes: Jamf has no direct equivalent; compliance is usually expressed through Smart Groups and Conditional Access integration.

toJamf.notes: Jamf Pro has no native compliance policy object. Device state feeds Conditional Access through the Jamf-Intune integration instead, which must be configured separately.

disruptionItems.title: FileVault recovery key re-escrow
disruptionItems.summary: Recovery keys stay with the source MDM. The destination cannot escrow a key it never issued, so every migrated Mac needs a new key issued and escrowed.
remediation: Escrow Buddy (Netflix, open source) automates re-issue and escrow at next login
Manual key import for BYOD or pre-encrypted devices
disruptionItems.edgeCase: macOS keeps using the original escrow certificate until FileVault is toggled off and on, so renewing the certificate alone will not fix a failed escrow.

disruptionItems.title: Certificate reissuance
disruptionItems.summary: Wi-Fi, VPN and 802.1X identities are issued by the source MDM's CA and do not transfer.
remediation: Stage the destination's certificate profiles before the ABM move
disruptionItems.edgeCase: Devices can land in the destination MDM with no network access if certificates are not ready first.

disruptionItems.title: Platform SSO re-registration
disruptionItems.summary: Users must re-register Platform SSO after the move, in either direction.
remediation: Communicate to users in advance; it resembles a failure otherwise
